title: Positioning and Finding Work
description: Describe what you do in a way that reaches the clients who need it and repels the ones who don't — a specific enough niche, the channels those clients actually use, outreach that gets read, proof you can show without naming names, and the discipline to decline work that will hurt you.

title: Contracts, Liability and Data
description: Know which contract terms matter in an AI automation engagement and which will hurt you later — the clauses worth negotiating, what happens when the automation gets something wrong, data processing terms in plain language, who owns the prompts and the pipeline, and when the answer to a legal question is 'get an actual lawyer.'

title: The Work You Won't Take
description: Decide in advance which engagements you refuse, and be able to say why without a speech — automations that quietly harm the people downstream, surveillance dressed as efficiency, decisions about people that shouldn't be automated at all, and the client who wants cover rather than advice.

title: Engagements That Survive a Missed Week
description: Structure the work so a bad fortnight doesn't cost you a client — deliverables that don't need you present, async-first engagements stated up front, buffers built into the plan instead of held in your head, what to actually tell a client when you can't work this week, and pricing that doesn't punish a slow week.

title: Staying Current Without Drowning
description: Keep your capability picture accurate on a small, fixed time budget — what actually changes and how often, which sources are worth reading and which are noise, testing a new capability in under an hour, updating advice you already gave a client, and a quarterly review of your own assumptions.
